source.title: Optimal scaling of average queue sizes in an input-queued switch: an open problem

accepted.question_text: For an n by n input-queued switch operating in discrete time, with n input ports and n output ports, each feasible schedule a matching between input and output ports, independent Bernoulli arrivals with rates λ_i,j, load factor ρ(λ) defined as the maximum over all input-row and output-column aggregate arrival rates, and Q*(n,λ) the minimum over all scheduling policies of the steady-state expected total queue size E[sum_i,j Q_i,j], what is β*_0, the infimum over positive exponents β for which there is a constant c > 0 such that Q*(n,λ) is at most c n^β divided by 1 − ρ(λ), uniformly for all n and all arrival-rate matrices λ with 0 < ρ(λ) < 1? In particular, is β*_0 equal to 1?

evidence.quote: Find β∗0, the infimum over all positive numbers β for which there exists a constant c > 0 such that Q∗(n,λ) ≤ c · nβ/(1 − ρ(λ)).

accepted.question_text: In the same n by n input-queued switch model with load factor ρ(λ) and optimal steady-state expected total queue size Q*(n,λ), what is β*_1, the infimum over positive β for which there is a constant c > 0 such that, for every fixed n, the heavy-traffic limit superior as ρ(λ) approaches 1 of (1 − ρ(λ)) Q*(n,λ) is at most c n^β? Is the value of this exponent 1?

evidence.quote: Find β∗1, the infimum over all positive numbers β for which there exists a constant c > 0 such that lim sup ρ(λ)→1 (1 − ρ(λ)) · Q∗(n,λ) ≤ c · nβ.
an intermediate (weaker) conjecture, such as β∗1 = 1, may be easier to prove.

accepted.question_text: In the same n by n input-queued switch model with load factor ρ(λ) and optimal steady-state expected total queue size Q*(n,λ), what is β*_2, the infimum over positive β for which there is a constant c > 0 such that, for every arrival-rate matrix λ with ρ(λ) < 1, the limit superior as n approaches infinity of Q*(n,λ)/n^β is at most c/(1 − ρ(λ))? Is this exponent equal to 1?

evidence.quote: Find β∗2, the infimum over all positive numbers β for which there exists a constant c > 0 such that lim sup n→∞ 1/nβ · Q∗(n,λ) ≤ c/(1 − ρ(λ)).
We conjecture that β∗0 = 1, which would also imply that β∗1 = 1 and β∗2 = 1.

accepted.question_text: For the maximum weight scheduling policy in the same n by n input-queued switch model, where each time slot chooses a feasible matching that maximizes the sum over scheduled queues of the current queue size, does the steady-state expected total queue size satisfy the same β*_0 = 1 scaling as the conjectured optimum, namely essentially order n/(1 − ρ(λ)) up to constants uniformly over all n and all underloaded arrival-rate matrices?

evidence.quote: The question is whether there exist policies that combine the best features of the above two bounds, i.e., with Q = O(n1+ε/(1 − ρ)) for arbitrarily small ε > 0, and whether this is achieved by the MW policy.
We also have the much stronger conjecture that β∗0 is equal to one even if we restrict to the MW policy.

accepted.question_text: For the same n by n input-queued switch model restricted to uniform traffic, where every input-output arrival rate is λ_i,j = ρ/n, what are the corresponding optimal and maximum-weight-policy queue-size scaling exponents for steady-state expected total queue size as functions of n and ρ, and do the β*_0, β*_1, and β*_2 questions have value 1 in this uniform-traffic case?

evidence.quote: In a further variation, the same questions can be posed for the case of uniform traffic, where λi,j = ρ/n, for all i and j.

accepted.question_text: When the load factor ρ is held fixed in the same input-queued switch setting, can a Markovian scheduling policy, whose action depends only on the current queue vector rather than the full past history, achieve steady-state expected total queue-size performance O(n^(1+ε)) for every ε > 0, matching the near-linear dependence in n suggested by batching policies without requiring a non-Markovian history-dependent rule?

evidence.quote: we conjecture this property to be true, so that Markovian policies can also deliver O(n1+ε) performance (for any ε > 0) when ρ is held fixed.
